concepts.term: Impact of the First World War
concepts.def: Military defeats, food shortages and inflation by 1917 destroyed faith in Tsar Nicholas II, who had taken personal command of the army in 1915.
Bread riots and strikes in Petrograd, joined by mutinying soldiers, forced Nicholas II to abdicate and ended Romanov rule.
Lenin's Bolsheviks seized power from the Provisional Government in Petrograd, promising 'Peace, Bread and Land'.
Harsh Civil War policy of grain requisitioning and nationalised industry that provoked peasant revolts and contributed to the famine of 1921.
Lenin's tactical retreat that allowed peasants to sell surplus grain and permitted small private trade to revive the shattered economy.
Stalin's drive from 1928 to industrialise the USSR rapidly, setting ambitious targets for coal, iron, steel and electricity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Russia 1914-41 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Russia 1914-41 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Russia 1914-41.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why did Nicholas II's decision to take personal command of the army in 1915 damage him?
options: He was personally blamed for defeats, while government at home fell under the influence of the Tsarina and Rasputin
It broke an agreement with Germany and triggered invasion
The army immediately mutinied and arrested him
It made the Duma the real government of Russia

mcqs.q: Which slogan summed up the Bolshevik promises of 1917?
options: 'Peace, Bread and Land'
'Liberty, Equality, Fraternity'
'War until Victory'
'God, Tsar and Fatherland'
The New Economic Policy
The Five-Year Plans
Collectivisation
Serfdom

mcqs.q: What was the main aim of Stalin's Five-Year Plans?
options: Rapid industrialisation of the USSR
Restoring private ownership of factories
Returning land to the nobility
Reducing the size of the Red Army

mcqs.q: Did the Bolsheviks overthrow the Tsar in October 1917?
options: Lenin and the Bolsheviks toppled Tsar Nicholas II in October 1917.
The Tsar was overthrown by a German army occupying Petrograd.
The NEP banned all private trade in the USSR.
No - Nicholas II abdicated during the February Revolution; in October the Bolsheviks overthrew the Provisional Government that had replaced him.

mcqs.q: Was the New Economic Policy a return to full capitalism?
options: The Five-Year Plans were abandoned after one year.
The NEP abandoned communism and restored capitalism in Russia.
No - small trade and peasant markets were allowed, but the state kept control of the 'commanding heights': heavy industry, banking and foreign trade.
The NEP banned all private trade in the USSR.

mcqs.q: Did the Five-Year Plans modernise the USSR without cost?
options: The Five-Year Plans transformed Soviet industry smoothly and at no human cost.
The Five-Year Plans were abandoned after one year.
The Tsar was overthrown by a German army occupying Petrograd.
No - output of coal, iron and steel rose dramatically, but figures were often falsified, quality was poor, and workers faced harsh discipline and dangerous conditions.
